name: Temozolomide, concurrent with radiation (Stupp concurrent phase)

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Central Nervous System Cancers (general reference)

institution.provenance: DRAFT decision-support protocol authored from standard guidelines (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: temozolomide is low-to-moderate emetic risk; a serotonin (5-HT3) antagonist about an hour before each dose is usually sufficient.

supportiveCare: Pneumocystis (PJP) prophylaxis during the concurrent daily phase because of prolonged lymphopenia (for example co-trimoxazole on a physician-set schedule).
Take on an empty stomach at a consistent time to limit nausea; give with radiation on radiation days.
Steroid and anti-seizure medication as clinically needed; not routine for all patients.
monitoring: CBC weekly during the concurrent phase (watch for lymphopenia and thrombocytopenia)
Neurologic status and post-radiation MRI to distinguish pseudoprogression from true progression

drugs.name: Temozolomide
drugs.notes: 75 mg/m2 by mouth once daily, every day (7 days per week) throughout the focal radiation course (about 6 weeks / 42 days), then a treatment break before adjuvant cycles. Concurrent daily dosing; day marker [1] denotes the start of a continuous daily schedule. Standard Stupp concurrent-phase dose (NCCN CNS / DeVita, general reference; own wording).
